```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

# Percent Green


## SALURBAL (BECGSPCT)

Let's first see what geographic levels this variables is available for

```{r}
#| code-summary: "SALURBAL"

## Connect to BEC database
salurbal_BEC__v2 = "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/salurbal_BEC__v2/salurbal_BEC__v2.parquet" |> 
   arrow::open_dataset() 

## Query for all BECGSPCT data
df_salurbal_BEC__v2__pct_green = salurbal_BEC__v2 |> 
    select(iso2, geo, salid, year, BECGSPCT) |> 
    filter(!is.na(BECGSPCT)) |> 
    collect()

## Preview
df_salurbal_BEC__v2__pct_green %>% 
  sample_n(10) %>% 
  head()
```


Just to see availability across country and geographic level. 

```{r}
df_salurbal_BEC__v2__pct_green %>% 
  count(iso2, geo) %>% 
  arrange(iso2)
```

Note that the `BECGSPCT` variable is cross sectional for SALURBAL with an unspecified year. But we will use the most granular available which is L3 for all three countries. 

## USA

Here we reference the [CCUH Percent Green dataset](https://www.notion.so/drexel-ccuh/NCLD-Percent-Greeness-Dataset-18a57008e8858036b531ce4f6c762bf7)

```{r}
#| code-fold: false

## Connect to database
ccuh_pct_green__v1 =  "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/fed_data_v1/ccuh_pct_green__v1.parquet" |> arrow::open_dataset() 

## Query
df_ccuh_pct_green__v1 = ccuh_pct_green__v1 |>collect()

## Preview
head(df_ccuh_pct_green__v1)
```

let see available across geographic levels and year.

```{r}
df_ccuh_pct_green__v1 %>% 
  count(geo, year) %>% 
  summarize(year = paste(unique(year), collapse = ','), .by = geo)
```


## Harmonization

So for percent green space we will use the most granular data available for SALURBAL and for Philadelphia. Lets pull and harmonize into a single data structure here.

```{r}

## SALURBAL
df_nbhd_pct_green_salurbal = df_salurbal_BEC__v2__pct_green %>% 
  filter(geo == 'L3') %>% 
  mutate(parent =  'SALURBAL BECGSPCT',
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>% 
  rename(pct_green = BECGSPCT, geoid = salid) 
  
## USA
df_nbhd_pct_green_usa = df_ccuh_pct_green__v1 %>% 
  filter(geo == 'tract10',
         geoid %in% vec__philadelphia_tracts,
         year == 2016) %>% 
  mutate(iso2 = 'USA - Philadelphia',
         parent = 'ccuh_pct_green__v1' ) %>% 
  select(iso2, geo, geoid, pct_green, parent)
  

## CCUH MS1
df_nbhd_pct_green = bind_rows(
  df_nbhd_pct_green_salurbal,
  df_nbhd_pct_green_usa
)
df_nbhd_pct_green %>% write_parquet(context$df_pct_green)
```

## QC

Quick visual isnpections

```{r}
df_nbhd_pct_green %>% 
  mutate(iso2_geo = glue::glue("{iso2} ({geo})")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = pct_green)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_density(color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~iso2_geo, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of % Green Space ",
    x = "Percentage of Green Space",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )
```


## Access

```{{r}}
df_pct_green =  "`r context$df_pct_green`" |> 
  arrow::open_dataset() %>% 
  arrow::collect()
```

# Education variables

## SALURBAL (CNSMINPR)


Let's first see what geographic levels this variables is available for

```{r}
#| code-summary: "SALURBAL"

## Connect to database
salurbal_SEC_Census__v1 = "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/salurbal_SEC_Census__v1/salurbal_SEC_Census__v1.parquet" |> 
   arrow::open_dataset() 

## Query for all CNSMINPR data
df_cnsminpr = salurbal_SEC_Census__v1 |>
   select(iso2, geo, salid, year, CNSMINPR) %>% 
   collect() %>% 
   filter(!is.na(CNSMINPR))

## Preview
df_cnsminpr %>% 
  sample_n(10) %>% 
  head()
```


Just to see availability across country and geographic level. 

```{r}
df_cnsminpr %>% 
  count(iso2, year, geo) %>% 
  arrange(iso2)
```

Note that the `CNSMINPR` variable is longitudinal for SALURBAL. But we will use the most granular available which is L3 for everythign but BR which is L2_5. Also we will pull just for more recent year available for each country.


## USA

Here we reference the [CCUH USA Neighborhood (ACS Dataset)](https://www.notion.so/drexel-ccuh/USA-Neighborhood-ACS-Dataset-15e57008e885804c8a73cdd75b618c34)

```{r}
#| code-fold: false

## Connect to database
acs_v1 = "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/acs_v1/acs__v1.parquet" |> 
  arrow::open_dataset()

## Query for two variables ACS_MINPR and pct_high_school
df_education_acs = acs_v1 %>% 
  select(geoid, year, geo, ACS_MINPR, pct_bachelors) %>% 
  collect() 

## Preview
head(df_education_acs)
```

let see available across geographic levels and year.

```{r}
df_education_acs %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ACS_MINPR, pct_bachelors)) %>% 
  count(geo, year, name) %>% 
  summarize(year = paste(unique(year), collapse = ','), 
            .by =c( geo, name))
```

## Harmonization

So for percent education atinament space we will use the most granular data available for SALURBAL and for Philadelphia. Lets pull and harmonize into a single data structure here.

```{r}

## SALURBAL
df_pct_primary_salurbal = df_cnsminpr  %>%
  filter(
    (iso2 %in% c("PA", "GT") & geo == "L3") |
    (iso2 == "BR" & geo == "L2_5")
  )  %>% 
  mutate(parent =  'salurbal_SEC_Census__v1',
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>% 
  rename(pct_primary = CNSMINPR, geoid = salid) 
  
## USA
df_pct_primary_philadelphia = df_education_acs %>% 
  filter(geo == 'tract',
         geoid %in% vec__philadelphia_tracts,
         year == 2016) %>% 
  mutate(iso2 = 'USA - Philadelphia',
         parent = 'acs_v1' ) %>% 
  select(iso2, geo, geoid, 
         pct_primary = ACS_MINPR, 
         parent)
  

## CCUH MS1
df_pct_primary = bind_rows(
  df_pct_primary_salurbal,
  df_pct_primary_philadelphia
)
df_pct_primary %>% write_parquet(context$df_pct_primary)
```

## QC

Quick visual inspection

```{r}
df_pct_primary %>% 
  mutate(iso2_geo = glue::glue("{iso2} ({geo})")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = pct_primary)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_density(color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~iso2_geo, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of % primary  ",
    x = "Percentage of primary ",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )
```


## Access

```{{r}}
df_pct_primary =  "`r context$df_pct_primary`" |> 
  arrow::open_dataset() %>% 
  arrow::collect()
```

# Population Density


## SALURBAL (BECPOPDENS)

Let's first see what geographic levels this variables is available for

```{r}
#| code-summary: "SALURBAL"

## Connect to BEC database
salurbal_BEC__v2 = "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/salurbal_BEC__v2/salurbal_BEC__v2.parquet" |> 
   arrow::open_dataset() 

## Query for all BECPOPDENS data
df_pop_dens_salurbal = salurbal_BEC__v2 |> 
    select(iso2, geo, salid, year, BECPOPDENS) |> 
    filter(!is.na(BECPOPDENS)) |> 
    collect()

## Preview
df_pop_dens_salurbal %>% 
  sample_n(10) %>% 
  head()
```


Just to see availability across country and geographic level. 

```{r}
df_pop_dens_salurbal %>% 
  count(iso2, geo) %>% 
  arrange(iso2)
```

Note that the `BECGSPCT` variable is cross sectional for SALURBAL with an unspecified year. But we will use the most granular available which is L3 for all three countries. 


## USA 

Here we reference the [CCUH USA Neighborhood (ACS Dataset)](https://www.notion.so/drexel-ccuh/USA-Neighborhood-ACS-Dataset-15e57008e885804c8a73cdd75b618c34)


```{r}
#| code-fold: false

## Connect to database
acs_v1 = "//files.drexel.edu/colleges/SOPH/Shared/UHC/Projects/CCUH/ccuh-server/freeze/acs_v1/acs__v1.parquet" |> 
  arrow::open_dataset()

## Query for two variables ACS_MINPR and pct_high_school
df_pop_dens_acs  = acs_v1 %>% 
  select(geoid, year, geo, population_density_per_sq_km) %>% 
  collect() 

## Preview
head(df_pop_dens_acs)
```

let see available across geographic levels and year.

```{r}
df_pop_dens_acs %>% 
  count(geo, year) %>% 
  summarize(year = paste(unique(year), collapse = ','), 
            .by =c( geo))
```


## Harmonization

So for percent green space we will use the most granular data available for SALURBAL and for Philadelphia. Lets pull and harmonize into a single data structure here.

```{r}

## SALURBAL
df_nbhd_pop_dens_salurbal = df_pop_dens_salurbal %>% 
  filter(geo == 'L3') %>% 
  mutate(parent =  'SALURBAL BECPOPDENS',
         year = as.numeric(year)) %>% 
  rename(population_density_per_sq_km = BECPOPDENS, geoid = salid) 
  
## USA
df_nbhd_pop_dens_usa = df_pop_dens_acs %>% 
  filter(geo == 'tract',
         geoid %in% vec__philadelphia_tracts,
         year == 2016) %>% 
  mutate(iso2 = 'USA - Philadelphia',
         parent = 'acs_v1' ) %>% 
  select(iso2, geo, geoid, population_density_per_sq_km, parent)
  

## CCUH MS1
df_nbhd_pop_dens = bind_rows(
  df_nbhd_pop_dens_salurbal,
  df_nbhd_pop_dens_usa
)
df_nbhd_pop_dens %>% write_parquet(context$df_nbhd_pop_dens)
```

## QC

Quick visual isnpections

```{r}
df_nbhd_pop_dens %>% 
  mutate(iso2_geo = glue::glue("{iso2} ({geo})")) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = iso2_geo, y = population_density_per_sq_km)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Population Density by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Population Density (per sq km)"

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
```
